newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat at standstill over pool uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat at standstill over pool uncertainty.

text.p: Australian wheat futures trading came to a halt on Monday as the market waited for the Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) pool price revision later in the day.
No trades took place in either futures or options.

The market freeze is over a gap between cash and pools prices, with the current estimated pools price for Australian Standard White (ASW) A$190.00 a tonne against the AWB's indicative domestic cash price for ASW delivered Newcastle of A$142.00 a tonne.
After allowing for differences in payment periods and other costs, this represents a gap of almost A$30.00 a tonne.
Monday's futures market was under the influence of pool price uncertainty, said Ben Suttie of C A & L Bell Commodities Corp Pty Ltd.
Suttie is predicting a pool price cut of A$5.00 a tonne but other brokers and traders are predicting a cut of A$10.00 to A$15.00 a tonne.
